components.title: Part 1 - Toasted Bread

ingredients.item: Arabic bread (pita), cut into 2 cm squares
ingredients.note: the source says 'as desired'; 1 loaf is enough for 2

prep: Turn the oven on to 180 C.
Cut 1 Arabic bread into 2 cm squares with a knife or kitchen scissors.
steps: Spread the bread squares on a baking tray in one layer and drizzle 1 tbsp olive oil over them. Toss with your hands so every piece is lightly coated.
Bake in the middle of the oven at 180 C for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp. They are ready when a piece snaps cleanly in your fingers.
Take the tray out and leave the bread to cool on the tray for 5 minutes so it stays crisp.

components.title: Part 2 - Vegetables and Pomegranate Dressing

ingredients.item: Purslane leaves, picked from the stems

ingredients.note: plus a pinch for the top

prep: Wash the lettuce, parsley, mint, purslane, radishes and green onion under cold running water. Dry the leaves in a salad spinner or roll them in a clean kitchen towel; wet leaves make the dressing slide off and the salad watery.

Cut the lettuce into 2 cm strips, the tomatoes into 2 cm cubes, the cucumbers into 1.5 cm cubes and the radishes into small cubes. Coarsely chop the parsley and mint, chop the green onion, and cut the green and red bell pepper into small cubes.
Squeeze the lemons and measure 2 tbsp juice. Crush 1 garlic clove.
steps: Put the lettuce, parsley, mint, radishes, cucumbers, tomatoes, green and red bell pepper, purslane and green onion in a large salad bowl and toss gently with two spoons for 30 seconds until the colours are evenly mixed.

In a small bowl whisk 1 crushed garlic clove, 1/4 cup olive oil, 2 tbsp pomegranate molasses, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper and 1 1/2 tsp sumac for 30 seconds until the dressing is dark, glossy and slightly thick.
Just before serving, pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently for 30 seconds until every leaf shines.
Transfer to a serving dish and scatter the toasted bread from Part 1 over the top. Sprinkle a pinch of sumac and serve at once while the bread is still crisp.

components.title: Part 1 - Walnut Salad with Pomegranate Dressing

ingredients.item: Tomato, large, cut into fine 5 mm cubes
Cucumber, cut into fine 5 mm cubes
Green bell pepper (sweet), small, very finely chopped

ingredients.note: the number is missing on the source page; 1 tbsp is used

prep: Wash the tomato, cucumber, green bell pepper, parsley and mint and dry them well.
Cut the tomato and cucumber into fine 5 mm cubes. Remove the seeds and white ribs from the green bell pepper and chop it very finely. Peel and chop the onion very finely.
Finely chop 2 tbsp parsley and 1 tbsp mint. Squeeze 1 lemon (about 3 tbsp juice).
Coarsely chop 1/2 cup walnuts into pea-size pieces.
steps: Put the chopped walnuts in a dry non-stick pan 24 cm over medium-low heat. Stir every 30 seconds for 3 to 4 minutes until they smell toasted and turn one shade darker. Tip them straight onto a plate and let them cool for 5 minutes so they do not keep cooking.
In a medium salad bowl combine the tomato, cucumber, green bell pepper and onion cubes. Add the 2 tbsp parsley and 1 tbsp mint.
In a small bowl stir 2 tbsp pomegranate molasses, 3 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil and 1/2 tsp salt for 20 seconds until the salt dissolves.
Just before serving, add the cooled walnuts to the bowl, pour the dressing over and mix well for 30 seconds until everything is coated and glossy. Taste and add a pinch of salt only if needed.

Walnuts soft and soggy -> add them only at the moment of serving.
Salad swimming in juice -> cut the tomato just before mixing and use firm tomatoes.
Onion too strong -> chop it very finely; if it is very sharp, rinse the chopped onion in cold water for 1 minute and drain well.
Too salty -> the source uses 1 tsp; this version uses 1/2 tsp, taste before adding more.
serving: Spoon the salad into a shallow bowl and scatter a few extra walnut pieces on top.

components.title: Part 1 - Light Corn Salad

ingredients.item: Sweet corn kernels, canned and drained (or frozen)

prep: Canned corn: open the can, pour the corn into a sieve, rinse under cold water for 20 seconds and leave to drain for 2 minutes.

Frozen corn: boil 2 cups of water in a small pot, add 1 1/2 cups frozen corn, cook for 3 to 4 minutes after the water boils again until the kernels are bright yellow and tender, then drain in the sieve and rinse under cold water until cool.
Peel and finely chop 1/2 medium onion. Wash, dry and finely chop 1 tbsp parsley.
steps: Put the drained corn, the chopped onion and 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar in a medium bowl and stir for 20 seconds so the onion softens in the vinegar.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil and 1/4 tsp salt and stir again for 20 seconds until every kernel is shiny.
Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge for 15 to 20 minutes until cold; the corn absorbs the dressing.
Stir once more, spoon into a serving dish and sprinkle the 1 tbsp chopped parsley on top. Serve cold.

mistakes: Salad watery -> drain the corn well in the sieve for the full 2 minutes before mixing.
Frozen corn hard or chewy -> boil 3 to 4 minutes after the water returns to the boil, then cool quickly.
Onion too strong -> chop it very finely and let it sit in the vinegar for the chilling time; this softens it.
Too salty -> canned corn often contains salt; rinse it and keep the added salt at 1/4 tsp.
serving: Serve cold in a small bowl with the parsley on top.

components.title: Part 1 - Lebanese Tabbouleh

ingredients.note: about 1 lemon; split into 1 tbsp + 1 tbsp

ingredients.item: Fresh mint leaves, very finely chopped
Tomatoes, cut into small 5 mm cubes
Sweet bell pepper, cut into small cubes

prep: Put 1/4 cup fine bulgur in a fine sieve and rinse under cold water for 10 seconds. Shake well, tip it into a small bowl and pour 1 tbsp of the lemon juice over it. Stir and leave to soak for 20 minutes.
Wash the parsley and mint very well in a large bowl of cold water, lift them out, then dry completely in a salad spinner or by rolling in a clean towel. Wet parsley turns to paste when chopped.
Pick the mint leaves from the stems. Cut off the thick lower parsley stems and discard them.
Wash and dry the tomato, bell pepper and lettuce leaves.
steps: Gather the parsley into a tight bundle on the board and slice it very finely across with a sharp knife, moving back about 2 mm each cut. Go over it once more to make it fine. You need about 2 cups. Chop the mint the same way (2 tbsp).
Cut the tomato into small 5 mm cubes, the onion into small cubes and the sweet bell pepper into small cubes.
After 20 minutes check the bulgur: bite a grain, it should be soft with only a slight chew. If it is still hard, add 1 tbsp of the tomato juice from the board and wait 5 more minutes.
In a large mixing bowl combine the tomatoes, onion, mint, parsley and soaked bulgur. Mix gently with your fingertips or two spoons for 30 seconds until evenly combined; do not squeeze.

Add 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, the sweet bell pepper and the remaining 1 tbsp lemon juice. Mix gently again for 30 seconds until all the green is shiny. Taste: it should be fresh and clearly lemony; add a pinch of salt if flat.
Line a serving dish with the 4 lettuce leaves, spoon the tabbouleh in the middle and serve at once.

mistakes: Parsley mushy and dark -> dry it completely before cutting, use a very sharp knife and never use a blender or food processor.
Bulgur hard and crunchy -> use fine bulgur, rinse it first and let it soak the full 20 minutes; add 1 tbsp tomato juice if it is still hard.
Salad watery -> cut the tomatoes small and add salt only at the end, just before serving.
Tabbouleh tastes flat -> it must be lemony; add 1 more tbsp lemon juice if needed.
Mixing too hard -> toss lightly with fingertips so the herbs stay fluffy, not pressed.
serving: Serve on a flat dish lined with crisp lettuce leaves; the leaves can be used as a scoop.
Tabbouleh is mostly green: the parsley should be the main ingredient, with tomato and bulgur as small specks.
Serve with grilled meat, falafel or as a mezze dish with hummus and Arabic bread.
safety: Wash hands before handling the vegetables. Use a clean board kept only for vegetables and fruit.
Wash all leaves and vegetables under cold running water and dry them well; wash herbs bunch by bunch and shake off the water.
Do not leave the dressed salad at room temperature for more than 2 hours (1 hour on a hot day).
Parsley grows close to the soil: wash it in 2 changes of water until no sand is left at the bottom of the bowl.
Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep 1 day in a closed container in the fridge but become soft.

spice_note: Source recipe contains no chili; black pepper is used only in the dressing at 1/8 tsp, and the chicken is seasoned with sweet paprika, garlic powder and lemon.

components.title: Part 1 - Grilled Chicken Breast
prep: Take the chicken out of the fridge 15 minutes before cooking. Do not wash raw chicken; pat it dry with paper towel and throw the towel away.

On the separate raw-chicken board, place each breast between two sheets of plastic wrap or baking paper and gently beat the thick end with a rolling pin until the whole breast is an even 1.5 cm thick.
In a bowl mix 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp sweet paprika and 1/4 tsp salt. Rub this over both sides of the chicken and leave for 10 minutes.
Wash the raw-chicken board, knife and your hands with hot soapy water.
steps: Heat the grill pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until a drop of water sizzles on it at once.
Lay the 2 chicken breasts in the pan and cook without moving for 5 to 6 minutes until the underside has clear golden-brown grill marks and releases easily.

Turn them with tongs and cook the second side over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes. Check the thickest part with a food thermometer: it must read 74 C. If there is no thermometer, cut the thickest part: the meat must be white all through with clear juices and no pink.
Move the chicken to a clean plate (not the raw-chicken plate) and rest for 5 minutes, then slice into 1 cm strips on the vegetable board after washing it.

components.title: Part 2 - Toasted Bread Cubes

ingredients.item: Toast bread slice, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

prep: Cut 1 slice of toast bread into 1.5 cm cubes.
steps: Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a non-stick pan 24 cm over medium heat for 30 seconds.
Add the bread cubes and stir every 30 seconds for 4 to 5 minutes until golden on all sides and crisp. Tip onto a plate to cool.

components.title: Part 3 - Caesar Dressing and Assembly
prep: Wash the lettuce leaf by leaf, dry well in a salad spinner or towel and chop coarsely into 3 to 4 cm pieces.
Grate 2 tbsp parmesan finely. Crush 1 garlic clove. Squeeze 2 tbsp lemon juice.
steps: In a small bowl whisk 1 1/2 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp lemon juice, the crushed garlic, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp black pepper until smooth.
Pour in the 6 tbsp olive oil slowly, about 1 tbsp at a time, whisking for 15 seconds after each addition, until the dressing is creamy and thick. Stir in the 2 tbsp parmesan.

Put the chopped lettuce and the sliced chicken in a large salad bowl. Pour about two thirds of the dressing over and toss for 30 seconds until every leaf is coated. Add the rest only if the salad looks dry.
Scatter the toasted bread cubes over the top and serve at once.

mistakes: Chicken dry outside and raw inside -> flatten it to an even 1.5 cm first and check 74 C in the thickest part.
Chicken sticks to the pan -> preheat the grill pan fully and do not move the chicken for the first 5 minutes.
Dressing oily and thin -> add the oil slowly while whisking; if it separates, whisk in 1 tsp more mayonnaise.
Bread cubes soft -> add them only on top at serving time.
Salad soggy -> dry the lettuce well and dress it just before serving.
Cross-contamination -> never cut the cooked chicken on the raw-chicken board or put it back on the raw plate.
serving: Pile the dressed lettuce in two wide bowls, fan the chicken strips on top and scatter the bread cubes.

Cool leftover chicken within 1 hour and keep it in a closed container in the fridge for 2 to 3 days.
The dressing contains mayonnaise and raw garlic: keep it in the fridge in a closed jar and use within 2 days.

safety: Wash hands before handling the vegetables. Use a clean board kept only for vegetables and fruit.
Wash all leaves and vegetables under cold running water and dry them well; wash herbs bunch by bunch and shake off the water.
Do not leave the dressed salad at room temperature for more than 2 hours (1 hour on a hot day).
Contains walnuts: check for nut allergy before serving to guests or children.
Washed undressed arugula keeps 2 days in the fridge wrapped in a damp towel inside a closed box; dressed salad should be eaten at once.
